one_line: Local-first canvas where an agent creates and edits vector design assets alongside a human.
what_it_does: LogoPacker is a browser design canvas with local asset access, agent activity, SVG generation, brand-guideline creation, and direct canvas editing.
leverage_rationale: The agent operates on structured live canvas state and local workspace assets, making repetitive multi-step vector edits more reliable than clicking through the UI.
leverage_evidence: About text describes direct access to local assets, selection state, visible canvas state, and autosave.
Frame sheets visibly show changing canvas content, an agent-working status, and editor controls.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a coherent canvas workflow from blank state through generated text/illustration and later edits, though end-to-end agent invocation and export are not directly evidenced.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show a consistent whiteboard editor with toolbar, canvas, properties/activity sidebar, and changing artwork.
Devpost packaging identifies a one-take hands-free demo and local workspace product.
impact_rationale: Designers and brand builders have a credible need to delegate repetitive variation, asset organization, and handoff preparation while retaining creative control.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets designers and repetitive design work.
Packet describes local fonts/assets, variations, layouts, and handoffs.
creativity_rationale: The local-first, agent-assisted editable canvas is a fresh synthesis with a meaningful human-in-the-loop interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Combines structured WebMCP editing with local workspace access.
Visible sequence shows agent-created illustration followed by direct user tuning.
usability_note: The visible editor has recognizable canvas controls, direct manipulation, and persistent activity/status feedback.
red_flags: No transcript and no directly visible tool-call invocation; much of the WebMCP behavior is claimed in text.
standouts: Local-first asset/font access is a concrete WebMCP advantage.
Canvas state visibly changes through a coherent creation-and-tuning flow.
advance_reason: Strong concept and visible product coherence, with meaningful structured-agent leverage despite incomplete invocation evidence.

one_line: Human-governed mission control where agents inspect evidence and propose, but do not approve, task transitions.
what_it_does: Mission Center exposes task state, dependencies, evidence, proposals, revalidation, and audit history to browser agents while requiring a human approval gate for lifecycle changes.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP exposes semantic task/evidence state and a proposal-only mutation model that a general UI-driving agent could not reproduce as reliably or safely.
leverage_evidence: About text specifies eight shared-state tools, proposal queue, revision/evidence gate, and audit trail.
The stated journey has the agent propose Review to Done while a human revalidates and approves.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a tightly scoped, intentional workflow with explicit state separation and verification, supported by deterministic tests and deployment claims; visual evidence is present but invocation details are not legible here.
execution_evidence: About text describes the complete Review → proposal → revalidate → human approval → Done flow.
Claims deterministic Node tests, verification scripts, browser storage, and deployed static app.
Frame sheets are submitted for the workflow.
impact_rationale: Teams coordinating agent work have a real need for evidence-backed, auditable automation that preserves human authority over consequential state changes.
impact_evidence: Pitch explicitly targets task inspection, evidence verification, and safe lifecycle actions.
Human approval and auditability address a concrete governance problem.
creativity_rationale: The proposal-only agent and human revalidation model is a notably original interaction pattern for browser-native mission control.
creativity_evidence: Separates agent proposals from human decisions as first-class auditable objects.
Revision-gated evidence approval is pursued as the central product interaction.
usability_note: The described review queue and explicit approval flow should be understandable, though detailed visual legibility is limited.
red_flags: Prior work disclosure says the competition edition derives from an existing Mission Center project; eligibility depends on challenge-new work not established in the packet.
standouts: Shared semantic state, evidence, and audit trail are central rather than decorative.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage and a clear, high-value governance workflow; eligibility should be checked separately because of disclosed prior work.

one_line: Agent-native vehicle configurator, synchronized garage twin, owner's guide, and 3D creation engine.
what_it_does: AutoLab lets agents inspect and revise a fictional vehicle build, calculate pricing, control a shared 3D model, reveal components, and inspect the measured creation workflow.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP spans multiple live product contexts and exposes precise structured configuration, vehicle state, measurements, undoable mutations, and revision gates that are difficult to drive reliably through a 3D UI.
leverage_evidence: About text claims 49 tools across landing, configurator, Garage, Owner's Guide, and Creation Engine.
Human interruption, revision-gated undoable mutations, and source/measurement-basis results are described.
execution_rationale: The scope is unusually broad but internally coherent, with a public repo, typed stack, testing technologies, and submitted frame sheets; the packet lacks transcript detail for every surface.
execution_evidence: About text names React/Three.js/Vite/Zod/Zustand plus Vitest and Playwright.
Public repository and live demo are reported alive.
Three frame sheets are submitted.
impact_rationale: Vehicle buyers, configurators, and enthusiasts can benefit from precise agent-assisted exploration of complex options, pricing, ownership outcomes, and technical documentation.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets configuring and understanding a shared car.
Product combines configurator, garage twin, guide, and measured 3D creation workflow.
creativity_rationale: The combination of an agent-operable vehicle configurator, synchronized digital twin, visual guide, and code-native measured 3D engine is ambitious and memorable.
creativity_evidence: Five page contexts and 49 tools pursue a deep cross-surface concept.
Independent reconstruction uses public dimensions/photos rather than manufacturer CAD.
usability_note: A large multi-context 3D product is inherently complex; stated undo, interruption, and source-basis feedback support control.
red_flags: Very broad scope and many claims are not individually verifiable from the supplied text and static frame evidence.
standouts: Deep structured control of a shared 3D vehicle state.
Measurement-driven creation workflow and safety semantics add substance beyond a configurator demo.
advance_reason: One of the packet's strongest combinations of ambitious concept and WebMCP-native 3D interaction.

one_line: AI-assisted fraud intelligence and social-engineering protection for African digital payments.
what_it_does: Ayib FraudGuard analyzes transaction and contextual signals for anomaly detection, behavioral analysis, social-engineering risk, scoring, and API-based fraud intelligence.
leverage_rationale: The packet describes an API-driven fraud product but provides little evidence of what WebMCP changes versus a conventional API or UI workflow.
leverage_evidence: About text emphasizes an API-based security layer and generic automation capabilities.
No video frame sheets were submitted and no concrete WebMCP tool/state workflow is shown.
execution_rationale: The stated product idea is coherent, but the packet has no submitted video frames and only sparse visible packaging evidence, so claimed completeness cannot be established.
execution_evidence: Live demo and public repo are reported in the facts.
Devpost text describes risk analysis capabilities but omits an evidenced end-to-end run.
impact_rationale: Fintechs, banks, marketplaces, and developers face a substantial real problem in payment fraud and socially engineered transfers, particularly in under-served markets.
impact_evidence: Inspiration identifies sophisticated fraud and the gap between transaction-only signals and social engineering.
Named intended audiences include fintechs, banks, payment platforms, marketplaces, and developers.
creativity_rationale: Applying contextual and social-engineering intelligence to African payment fraud is a meaningful angle, though the described product category is established.
creativity_evidence: Focuses on context around apparently legitimate transactions.
Regional framing is specific rather than generic fraud tooling.
usability_note: Insufficient visual/product evidence to assess the actual user workflow.
red_flags: WebMCP-specific implementation and live workflow are not evidenced in the packet.
standouts: Concrete high-stakes problem and regionally specific audience.
advance_reason: Potentially valuable fraud concept, but WebMCP leverage and execution are too weakly evidenced for advancement.

one_line: Stale-write protection for browser-agent pharmacy refills with human-reviewed order receipts.
what_it_does: ExactCue lets an agent prepare a refill, gives a person an exact versioned summary to review, and commits only when the pharmacy record still matches the reviewed version.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is used to expose only currently valid tools and shared live order state, while version/ETag checks make stale consequential writes fail instead of silently retrying.
leverage_evidence: About text documents pharmacy record v1 to v2 causing HTTP 409 and no write.
The reviewed cue includes prescriptions, pickup, record version, and fingerprint; current actions produce authoritative receipts.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a narrow, coherent, safety-critical workflow with explicit stale and successful outcomes; frame sheets are submitted, though no transcript is provided.
execution_evidence: About text describes prepare → exact human review → atomic server check → receipt/block flow.
Three frame sheets are submitted and the product/demo is reported live.
The stated 409 no-write behavior is a concrete failure-state design.
impact_rationale: Patients and caregivers have a real need for convenient refill preparation without an agent submitting an order that is no longer the one they reviewed.
impact_evidence: Specific pharmacy-refill audience and consequential stale-record problem.
Solution directly prevents an outdated refill from being committed.
creativity_rationale: The exact reviewed cue plus atomic stale-write block is a crisp, memorable interaction pattern for safe browser agents.
creativity_evidence: Uses a synthetic refill to demonstrate a general consequential-action pattern.
Combines visible, spoken, machine-readable review with authoritative receipt or refusal.
usability_note: The single exact cue, explicit version, and clear success/block result make the safety flow understandable.
red_flags: Synthetic pharmacy data and absent transcript limit observed proof of the live agent path.
standouts: Excellent stale-state failure mode with no-write guarantee.
Clear generalizable pattern for consequential browser actions.
advance_reason: Exceptionally strong WebMCP delta, real safety value, and a well-defined demonstrated workflow.

one_line: Source-grounded contract decision room where agents propose risk actions and humans approve them.
what_it_does: ClauseProof ingests local contracts with OCR, anchors findings to governing clauses, supports risk decisions, and prepares unsigned signature-packet receipts without collapsing approval into model output.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools expose case summary, clause-linked risks, proposals, human decisions, and unsigned packet preparation over the same live state, materially improving reliability and provenance.
leverage_evidence: About text lists six narrow tools and closed schemas with structured receipts.
Agent proposals remain proposals; approval requires visible human decision and signature preparation reports sent:false and signed:false.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a complete document-to-decision workflow with local OCR, deterministic rules, durable audit events, and explicit safety states; visual evidence is submitted but not transcribed.
execution_evidence: Synthetic agreement demonstrates multiple concrete findings: renewal, exclusivity, payment, cure, liability.
Claims React/TypeScript, PDF.js, Tesseract.js, Xano endpoints, audit receipts, and idempotent bootstrap.
Three frame sheets are submitted.
impact_rationale: Legal, procurement, and operations teams have a real need to find contract risks and coordinate decisions without mistaking AI analysis for authorization.
impact_evidence: Source-grounding keeps exact governing clauses beside findings.
Human resolution/acceptance and unsigned packet controls address consequential contract workflows.
creativity_rationale: The decision-room model, clause-level provenance, and explicit separation of analysis, proposal, approval, and signature preparation are a fresh synthesis.
creativity_evidence: Local OCR plus deterministic clause rules are integrated with agent tools.
Unsigned/sent:false receipts make the authority boundary concrete.
usability_note: The staged workflow is safety-conscious, though contract review can remain cognitively dense.
red_flags: Synthetic contract and absent transcript limit proof of broader document robustness.
standouts: OCR and deterministic clause evidence make the concept concrete.
advance_reason: High-value, well-specified human-agent contract workflow with strong structured-state leverage.

leverage_rationale: Structured shopping intent and product/shipping queries can reduce UI friction, but the packet does not show a deeply stateful or reliable delta beyond an agent-facing storefront layer.

one_line: Agent compiles a reviewed WASI deployment intent into verified browser and edge capsules with a bounded portability proof.
what_it_does: UNIV Deploy validates target compatibility, emits digest-bound capsules, executes on browser and edge, compares declared observations, and stores/rechecks a durable receipt.
leverage_rationale: Typed WebMCP tools carry a stateful, consequential multi-step deployment contract with opaque proof artifacts, bounded execution, and verification that a generic UI-driving agent could not reliably reproduce.
leverage_evidence: Transcript describes five typed tools, closed manifests, deterministic verification, capsule digests, and no shell/upload/arbitrary code.
Adversarial network-bound release yields empty frontier and no capsule; portable release yields two verified executions and matching output.
execution_rationale: The 99-second video transcript and frame sheets describe and visibly support a complete adversarial-to-success workflow, including verification, execution, output equality, durable storage, and retrieval checks.
execution_evidence: Video transcript explicitly reports the negative network case and successful two-target execution.
Transcript reports 2/2 matching observations and D1 receipt integrity checks.
Public repo, live demo, and video are reported.
impact_rationale: Release and security teams have a concrete need to test portability and provide evidence without granting agents dangerous shell or arbitrary execution access.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets platform, release, and security teams.
The system proves a bounded claim rather than making an unsafe universal portability promise.
creativity_rationale: The adversarial compiler plus verified target capsules and durable portability witness is an ambitious, memorable deployment interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Explicit counterexample frontier prevents invalid handoff.
Separates enforced, observed, build-pinned, and unattested facts in the receipt.
usability_note: The reviewer-facing proof model is clear, though deployment verification is inherently technical.
red_flags: Portability proof is deliberately bounded to the governed targets and observation contract, not universal portability.
standouts: Excellent adversarial demonstration and honest negative result.
Durable, independently rechecked proof artifact is unusually strong.
advance_reason: Top-tier evidence-backed execution and transformative WebMCP leverage with a technically ambitious, safety-bounded concept.

leverage_rationale: WebMCP makes a personal agent a live participant in the same authoritative multiplayer match through human-approved pairing, progressive tools, and filtered game state.

execution_evidence: Live demo and public repo are reported alive.

impact_evidence: Explicit audiences include players and agent builders.
Modes support teammate, opponent, and spectator competition use cases.
creativity_rationale: Bringing a player's existing AI agent into a real-time multiplayer combat arena is highly memorable and explores agent-mediated entertainment deeply.
creativity_evidence: Human-agent multiplayer is built into the game loop rather than appended as a chatbot.
Agent Cup and remote pairing broaden the interaction model.

one_line: Privacy-control layer where agents prepare exact changes and people approve, apply, and verify them.
what_it_does: ClearRights models website privacy choices for agents, creates an exact plan, requires unchanged human approval, applies it, reads it back, and issues a verified receipt.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP exposes a structured privacy model and exact reviewed plan while preserving a human hold and verification boundary that prevents agents from accepting intrusive banners by default.
leverage_evidence: About text describes exact plan preparation, deliberate human hold, unchanged-plan application, readback, and verified receipt.
Timeline separates agent preparation/application from human review and direct choices.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a complete prepare-review-apply-verify flow with reversible display preferences and submitted frame sheets; the lack of transcript lowers certainty about observed invocation.
execution_evidence: Product narrative specifies the full state transition and verified receipt.
Six gallery images and three frame sheets are reported.
Human-controlled privacy banner and timeline are described.
impact_rationale: Internet users have a widespread real problem: privacy choices are fragmented and browser agents may accept banners merely to continue. ClearRights directly addresses consent integrity.
impact_evidence: Inspiration identifies everyday cookie/privacy-control fragmentation and agent auto-accept risk.
The solution preserves the person's final authority and makes applied state verifiable.
creativity_rationale: Applying structured agent collaboration to privacy consent, with exact-plan locking and verified readback, is a fresh and socially meaningful interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Privacy choices become a shared structured state rather than a banner click.
Exact unchanged-plan hold is a concrete novel safety mechanism.
usability_note: The prepare/review/apply timeline and reversible display preferences should make the otherwise fragmented privacy flow legible.
red_flags: No transcript; the supplied evidence does not directly show agent invocation details.
standouts: Addresses a common harmful browser-agent default behavior.
Verified readback and exact-plan locking make the human boundary operational.
advance_reason: Strong real-world impact and a clear, safety-relevant WebMCP-native workflow.
